item.title: Shoulder Elevation MWM
clinicalUse: Painful shoulder elevation with an immediate correctable sign
patientPosition: Sitting or standing if safe, so active elevation can be reproduced.
contact: Broad contact or belt around proximal humerus depending on direction.
forceDirection: Commonly posterolateral or lateral corrective glide while patient elevates; exact direction is found clinically.
dosage: 6–10 reps × 2–3 sets when pain-free and beneficial.
mistakes: Using force instead of finding correct direction.
item.visualCue: Corrective humeral glide + active elevation → Retest elevation without glide.

subTechniques.name: Lateral Glide + Active Elevation
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Restore a painful/restricted elevation movement when a sustained lateral glide makes the motion immediately easier.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Standing or sitting with the shoulder girdle relaxed and the movement to be re-tested clearly defined.
subTechniques.contact: Use a belt or broad manual contact to sustain a lateral glide of the humeral head while the patient controls the arm.
subTechniques.direction: Maintain the pain-free glide while the patient actively elevates the arm. Adjust the glide direction until the movement is clearly improved or abandon the technique.
subTechniques.dosage: 6–10 repetitions for 2–3 sets if the PILL response is present.
subTechniques.reassess: Pain-free flexion/abduction and the exact reaching task.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: Mulligan's practical rule is PILL: Pain-free, Immediate improvement, Long-lasting effect. If the first two are absent, change or stop the technique.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Do not push through pain to complete repetitions.
